messages.subject: WISP and run.FShake3D = Create density surface with mouse manipulations
parts:
Hi, I am trying to generate a density surface in WISP using the mouse as it is mentioned in the command  run.FShake3D.

However, I call the command and nothing happens....Am I missing something?

The help index of WISP has several commands related to this function but all drives you to only one help. is something missing in help?

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: RE: [distance-sampling] WISP and run.FShake3D = Create density surface with mouse manipulations
parts:
Adrian:

I see you had downloaded WiSP yesterday.  I'm afraid FShake3D is not compatible with the more recent versions (>3.0) of R.  You still have the functionality of creating an undulating density surface via the use of the "add.hotspot()" function; that is not as visually interactive, but does provide the ability to make quite complex density surfaces.

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: RE: [distance-sampling] WISP and run.FShake3D = Create density surface with mouse manipulations
parts:
Adrian:

You are really giving WiSP a battering; happy to see it.

a) The answer to your questions about "exposure" is that the exact exposure values are irrelevant, and as you suspected the values are relative and their degree of variability is what matters.  b) It is indeed the case that a WiSP object of class 'population' contains what you seek.  Here is a quote from the help on generate.population()

generate.population returns an object of class 'population´ which has the following elements:

region

object of class 'region´
groupID

vector of identification numbers for the animal groups.
posx

vector of x-positions of the animal groups.
posy

vector of y-positions of the animal groups.
groupsize

vector of sizes of the animal groups.
ntypes

number of possible type properties for the animal groups.
types

vector of type properties of the animal groups.
minexposure

lowest possible group exposure value.
maxexposure

highest possible group exposure value.
exposure

vector of exposure values of the animal groups.
parents

Details of WiSP objects passed to function
created

Creation date and time
seed

Equal to the argument 'seed' passed to the function


I am inclined to suggest that you have a look at the DSsim package on CRAN (http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/DSsim/index.html)  It is specifically intended to perform the types of simulation that you seem to be initiating.  See if it might be more suited to your needs.

Well... its a nice fun for a Friday afertnoon.

Regarding the output, I´ve found that the commnand dput() produces the otuput of a text file where you can find the three needed fields:

posx
posy
group size.

Even when the x and y coordinates are only relevant to the artificial landscape we created (coordinates start at 0), the text file can be transferred and  modified to accomodate any GIS software. 

Will explore DsSim later

Many thanks again!
